You are producing a HEAD-TO-HEAD across business categories to find the BEST acquisition for Hooman at up to ~$500K all-cash. He has relaxed time (willing to go full-time / quit his job) and wants the best deal regardless of type (NOT just SaaS). He is a CANADIAN citizen (likely NO SBA leverage — weigh financing feasibility). Skills: AI/ML, data eng, cloud/infra, EE, strong diligence.

All categories + real deals found (JSON):
{
  "categories": [
    {
      "category": "SaaS / Software / Apps",
      "economics": "Typical fair multiple for real cash-flowing vertical B2B SaaS in the sub-$600K band is ~2.5x–3.5x SDE (BizBuySell self-reported software averages: ~2.06x revenue / ~3.60x earnings; median software asking price ~$1.0M, so this band is below-median, established-but-small assets). Micro-SaaS on Empire Flippers/Acquire commonly ~30–40x monthly profit (~2.5x–3.3x annual). At a fair ~3.0x SDE, a $500K all-cash buy yields ~$165K SDE ≈ $13–14K/month pre-tax, ~33% cash-on-cash — the best cash yield of any category IF revenue is durable. Owner-hours: true product SaaS with a contractor ~10–25 hr/wk; but the band is heavy with \"SEO/agency-as-SaaS\" listings that are full-time service shops (30–50 hr/wk). Warning: many sub-$600K \"SaaS\" listings are services in disguise or have declining revenue, cutting durable yield well below headline.",
      "financing": "SBA 7(a)/504 is realistically OFF THE TABLE. SBA SOP 50 10 requires the operating business to be ≥51% owned by US citizens or lawful permanent residents; a Canadian citizen with no US green card generally cannot use standard SBA leverage. Since nearly all listings here are US-based, most US bank acquisition financing is also unavailable to him — verify his exact residency status before assuming any US-loan path. Canadian options (BDC, Canadian banks) finance acquisitions but strongly prefer a Canadian-domiciled target with Canadian cash flow, so they are a poor fit for buying a US software company. Practical reality: treat every deal as ALL-CASH within ~$500K, with a SELLER NOTE / vendor take-back (10–30%, paid from the business's own cash flow) as the only realistic leverage — a seller note requires no citizenship and aligns seller incentives. The strongest in-band picks (EH&S SDS $325K, email SaaS $345K, EF #94153 $377K) fit all-cash with buffer; the $500K healthcare deals fit all-cash with no buffer.",
      "fit": "Best-mapped category to his skills. Real edge: (1) diligence alpha — he can read the codebase, evaluate churn/cohort data, judge AI-commoditization risk, and assess infra cost/scalability far better than a typical searcher; (2) value creation — for a stagnant vertical SaaS (EH&S/SDS, email provider) he can modernize the stack, add AI features, cut infra cost, and re-accelerate growth, which is exactly the improvable durable asset the mandate wants. His edge is IRRELEVANT/a trap on: the SEO/agency \"recurring revenue\" listings that dominate this band (really full-time service shops), and consumer AI-wrapper apps (thin moat — his own knowledge says model providers eat the feature). Willingness to go full-time unlocks owner-operated vertical SaaS, but the best-fit deals (A, B) run ~part-time with one contractor, leaving room to build rather than just operate.",
      "verdict": "STRONG vein — arguably the single best category for Hooman specifically, because it maximizes his two edges (technical/code diligence + AI/infra value creation) and delivers the best cash-on-cash yield per dollar (~33% at a fair 3x SDE all-cash). It also fits the all-cash-only Canadian reality: real durable sub-$500K vertical B2B SaaS trades at ~3x SDE and is buyable outright with cash to spare. Best sub-play: boring, bootstrapped, regulation-adjacent VERTICAL B2B SaaS at ~3x SDE (EH&S/SDS compliance software; long-lived email-service-provider SaaS) — sticky recurring revenue, mandate-driven demand, diversified customers, fairly priced, improvable by an AI/infra engineer. Avoid within the category: consumer AI-wrapper apps (commoditizable by model providers), \"SaaS\" that is really an SEO/service agency (owner-labor-dependent, no tech edge), declining-revenue assets sold at a fake \"discount\", and ARR-priced growth stories at 15–20x SDE.",
      "deal_count": 8
    },
    {
      "category": "E-commerce / DTC brands / Amazon FBA",
      "economics": "This category prices on SDE/net-profit multiples, NOT revenue. Empire Flippers quotes multiples in MONTHS of net profit; live listings on 2026-07-03 ran 26x-37x monthly = ~2.2x-3.1x annual SDE. BizBuySell's asking/cash-flow implied ~1.5x-4.5x SDE. Typical clean buy is ~2.0-3.0x SDE. A ~$500K all-cash purchase at ~2.5x buys roughly $165K-$250K annual SDE = ~$14K-$21K/mo pre-tax owner cash flow. Paper cash yield is very high (33-50%), but that discount is the market pricing in real decay risk. Owner-hours: 20-40+/wk for a genuine single-brand FBA business (inventory, PPC, suppliers, reviews); full-time for multi-store ops. \"Turnkey/automated\" hour claims are marketing.",
      "financing": "SBA 7(a) (10% down, 90% financed) is the entire leverage engine of the US FBA-acquisition market, and Hooman as a CANADIAN citizen almost certainly cannot use it. This removes the standard playbook but is actually an ADVANTAGE for an all-cash buyer: SBA-dependent bidders get frozen out of sub-$700K deals when credit tightens, and sellers prize a fast all-cash close. He can comfortably buy any listing here within $500K all-cash. Seller notes/earnouts are standard AND strongly advisable in this category — structure 30-50% as a seller note tied to trailing revenue to shift decay risk to the seller (the single biggest lever). Canadian banks/BDC will generally NOT lend against a US Amazon FBA account (intangible, foreign-platform collateral), so treat this as all-cash + seller-note only. Buying on Amazon US needs a US entity/EIN and sales-tax handling (~$5-15K setup + accounting).",
      "fit": "Strong on the improvement levers: PPC/ad optimization, keyword/listing data analysis, demand forecasting, inventory/reorder automation, and internal tooling are exactly what separates a well-run FBA brand from a decaying one — his data/AI/EE background is genuine value-creation, not decoration. BUT his edge is irrelevant to the actual moat, which is brand, reviews, supplier relationships, and Amazon goodwill — no ML fixes a suspended Seller Central account. Owner-dependence sits in supplier relationships and account health, both of which transfer with real handover risk. Full-time hands-on ownership is realistic and in-scope for him.",
      "verdict": "Weak-to-moderate vein for the BEST ~$500K buy. Highest headline yield and easiest all-cash fit of any category, but the WORST durability: single-brand Amazon FBA is a platform-dependent single-point-of-failure (account suspension, review purge, PPC/fee inflation, Chinese copycats, Amazon policy changes). The low 2-3x multiples are earned, not a bargain. Best sub-play: an aged (5+yr), multi-channel brand with real off-Amazon revenue (own Shopify + TikTok Shop), diversified SKUs, defensible brand/IP, bought all-cash at <=2.5x SDE with a LARGE seller note/earnout to offload decay risk onto the seller. On a risk-adjusted basis this should rank below cash-flowing service/'boring' businesses.",
      "deal_count": 7
    },
    {
      "category": "Content sites / newsletters / media / communities",
      "economics": "Cheapest multiples of any category, so $500K buys the most headline cash flow — but durability is the worst. Content/SEO/affiliate sites: ~2.0-3.5x SDE (28-42x monthly). YouTube channels: ~2.2-3.3x annual (27-40x monthly), 84-92% margins. Paid newsletters: 3-5x SDE. B2B niche media: 4-6x+ SDE/EBITDA. Communities/membership: 3-5x SDE. BizBuySell 'websites & ecommerce' benchmarks (607 listings, 2026-07-03): median asking $750K, median SDE $247,487, median earnings multiple 3.00x, median revenue multiple 0.75x. A ~$500K all-cash buy at the cheap end (~3x) yields ~$150-180K SDE/yr ≈ $12-15K/mo (highest monthly cash of any category at this budget) but often DECLINING on pure-SEO/single-platform assets; at the durable end (~4.5x newsletter/B2B media) ~$110K SDE/yr ≈ $9K/mo but a real, growable asset. Owner-hours: 10-25 hr/wk for content/YouTube, up to full-time for B2B media/community. The multiple you pay is inversely correlated with how fast the asset is melting.",
      "financing": "SBA is largely MOOT here — nearly all attractive deals FIT ALL-CASH within $500K (content sites, single YouTube channels, small newsletters), so the Canadian/no-SBA constraint is NOT a real handicap in this category (a genuine advantage vs. HVAC/laundromat). Digital-asset marketplaces (Empire Flippers, Flippa, Investors Club, LetterTrader) are cross-border friendly — sellers are frequently non-US, buyers global, and EF escrows the migration; no residency barrier to buy. Strongly recommend structuring 20-40% as a performance-based SELLER NOTE / earnout tied to trailing-12-mo profit on any content or YouTube deal, so the seller shares AI-Overview/algorithm downside. The only deal needing financing (Vancouver clean-energy media, $2.4M) is Canadian-domiciled, so BDC / Canadian bank acquisition financing is plausible — but it's 5x over budget. Do not count on SBA anywhere in this category.",
      "fit": "HIGH for operating; the constraint is asset quality, not his capability. His AI/ML + data-engineering skills are a rare, genuine value-creation edge: AI content pipelines (EF #95344 already runs on Claude/ElevenLabs/MidJourney — he'd run it better), programmatic/data-driven content, SEO recovery via structured data, newsletter automation, audience analytics. Most content-site sellers are non-technical marketers, so his diligence + tooling is real alpha. Where his edge is IRRELEVANT: it can't fix a structurally-declining SEO asset Google has deprioritized, and it doesn't create the audience relationships / sponsor rolodex that make B2B media and communities durable. Solo-runnable at this size (moderate owner-hours); he can go full-time or run alongside. Net: he should buy the MOAT (first-party list / community / brand) and then apply his tech edge — not buy a melting SEO asset hoping tech saves it.",
      "verdict": "Weak-to-moderate vein for the single BEST ~$500K buy. It offers the highest headline cash-on-cash yield at this budget and fits all-cash (no SBA issue), and Hooman's technical skills are a real operating edge — but the pure SEO/affiliate/YouTube assets are declining, AI-exposed (Google AI Overviews + Helpful Content updates gutted informational-site traffic), and command cheap multiples for good reason. This is a melting-ice-cube asset class unless the moat is a first-party audience, community, or brand. NOT where I'd expect the best durable ~$500K acquisition to come from. Best sub-play: a B2B niche newsletter or community with a first-party email list/membership (owns distribution, AI-safe) — inquire on LetterTrader's gated AI-newsletter listing and Quiet Light B2B-media deals — OR a genuinely brand/community-moated content site bought at a discount with a seller note that shares the AI-Overview downside, then defended/grown with his AI+data tooling. Avoid single-platform faceless YouTube (see #95833's -28% trend) and pure informational SEO sites with no email capture. Rule: distribution moat first, cash-flow multiple second.",
      "deal_count": 5
    },
    {
      "category": "Local service businesses (home & trades) — HVAC, plumbing, electrical, landscaping, cleaning, pest control, pool service, restoration, junk removal",
      "economics": "BizBuySell medians (fetched 2026-07-03): HVAC/plumbing 2.81x SDE / 0.67x rev, median SDE $236,775 (479 listings); landscaping 2.56x SDE / 0.79x rev, median SDE $180,000 (~611–818 listings); pest control 2.10x SDE / 0.86x rev, median SDE $189,576; pool service 2.48x SDE / 0.80x rev, median SDE $150,000; restoration 1.62x SDE / 0.48x rev, median SDE $358,708 (164 listings). Typical range 2.1–2.8x SDE (restoration cheaper because lumpy/insurance-driven). A ~$500K all-cash buy at ~2.3x SDE implies ~$180–220K annual SDE = ~$15–18.3K/mo owner cash and a ~35–45% pre-tax cash yield on equity; if you hire a GM to replace the owner, net drops to roughly $110–150K/yr (~$9–12.5K/mo) and ~25–30% yield. Owner-hours: route/recurring (pool/lawn/pest/cleaning) ~30–50 hr/wk and genuinely delegable to techs; trades (HVAC/plumbing/electrical) 40–60 hr/wk and license-holder-dependent; restoration on-call/lumpy.",
      "financing": "As a Canadian citizen / non-US person, Hooman almost certainly CANNOT use SBA 7(a)/504 — SBA requires ≥20% owners to be US citizens or green-card holders; a work-visa holder (TN/H-1B via Adobe) generally does not qualify. This removes the standard US '10% down + SBA covers 90%' leverage that most of these US asking prices implicitly assume, so FLAG it on every US deal. Practically he is an all-cash buyer: with $500K he cleanly covers the ~$150–220K SDE tier (2–2.5x) outright, and cash offers can win on speed/price. To reach the $500–700K tier (e.g. the OKC $317K-SDE pest deal, Moore OK lawn, FL HVAC) he needs SELLER FINANCING / vendor take-back — common in this category and offered on several listings (bed-bug deal advertises bank financing; Mosquito Shield offers owner financing). Target 50–60% cash down + 40–50% seller note over ~5 yrs; the SDE easily services it. If instead he buys a business IN CANADA, financing is materially easier: BDC and the Canada Small Business Financing Program (CSBFP) plus major-bank acquisition lending are open to citizens. ACTION: verify his exact US visa/residency status before assuming any US-loan path; if buying US, plan around all-cash + seller note.",
      "fit": "Good fit IF he targets route/recurring, no-license models (pool, lawn, pest, window/commercial cleaning). His AI/ML + data-engineering edge is a real margin lever there: most incumbents run on paper/spreadsheets, so route-density optimization, automated dispatch/scheduling, dynamic pricing, churn/renewal prediction, and review-generation automation create genuine value — plus his diligence/analytical ability lets him find mispriced deals (the ~1x-SDE wildlife listings and ~1.2x FL-HVAC outlier are either bargains or hiding something and warrant hard diligence). Where his edge is IRRELEVANT: local labor management (hiring/retaining/replacing techs, no-shows, turnover) is the real daily grind and is not a software problem; and trade licensing (HVAC/plumbing/electrical) is a hard blocker his EE degree doesn't solve — he'd need to retain the seller as qualifying party or hire a license-holder. It's also fully local/physical/owner-present (opposite of remote SaaS), requiring presence in the market — acceptable since he's willing to go full-time, but a real lifestyle shift.",
      "verdict": "Strong vein — arguably the best 'boring cash flow' category at $500K: cheap 2.1–2.8x SDE multiples, 30–45% cash yields, durable AI-safe demand, deep supply. Two Hooman-specific gates decide it: (1) avoid license-gated trades (his EE degree does NOT grant an HVAC/plumbing/electrical contractor license) and pick a no-license route model; (2) SBA leverage is off the table for him, so plan all-cash or a seller note. Best sub-play: a RECURRING ROUTE business — residential pest control (lowest recurring multiple at 2.10x, applicator license is exam-attainable) or pool-service route — with 150+ recurring accounts, ~$180–220K SDE, ~2.0–2.5x, seller carrying 40–50%. Concrete targets: OKC pest ($650K/$317K SDE, needs note), Camden NJ pest ($500K/$180K, 1000+ contracts, all-cash), Exton PA bed-bug ($450K/$192K), and the pool routes ($257–275K, all-cash). Runner-up is HVAC for raw SDE, but only viable if he locks a licensed qualifier and finances the higher ticket — a harder path for a Canadian cash buyer.",
      "deal_count": 10
    },
    {
      "category": "Physical / real-asset businesses, semi-absentee (laundromats, self-storage & RV/boat storage, car washes, vending/ATM routes)",
      "economics": "Live BizBuySell category medians (2026-07-03): LAUNDROMATS median ask $554,400 / rev $320,040 / SDE $116,475 (~4.8x headline, real deals 3-5x cash flow; all-cash yield ~15-25%; genuinely semi-absentee, ~5-15 owner hr/wk). SELF-STORAGE median ask $950,000 / rev $1,211,600 / SDE $245,000, but trades on CAP RATE not SDE — quality facilities sell at 5.3-7.4% caps (13-19x NOI, i.e. real-estate-priced $1M+); all-cash yield only ~6% unlevered; most passive of the group. CAR WASHES median ask $1,500,000 / rev $681,213 / SDE $210,235 (~7.1x, dragged up by express tunnels + RE); self-serve/coin bays trade 3-4x SDE and are cheaper; all-cash yield ~20-28% but volatile, maintenance-heavy, weather- and competition-exposed. VENDING/ATM median ask $145,000 / rev $154,000 / owner earnings $76,300 (~1.9x SDE) — cheapest and most cash-fit, yields look high (~30-50%) but low moat, churny locations, ATM in secular decline. A ~$500K all-cash laundromat at ~3x SDE ≈ ~$13-16K/mo owner cash flow; a self-serve car wash similar; storage at a 6% cap on $500K ≈ only ~$2,500/mo.",
      "financing": "CRITICAL: SBA 7(a)/504 is OFF the table for Hooman. As of March 2025 (Executive Order 14159) the SBA banned non-citizens/non-permanent-residents from SBA-guaranteed loans; the prior rule that let foreign nationals own <=49% and still qualify was eliminated. A Canadian citizen with no US green card CANNOT use the standard '10% down + SBA' leverage that most US laundromat/car-wash/storage buyers rely on. Consequences and alternatives: (1) Model every US deal as ALL-CASH <=$500K, or (2) SELLER FINANCING / VENDOR TAKE-BACK — common in this category, sellers routinely carry 20-50% over 3-7 years; this is Hooman's single most important lever and lets a ~$700-900K asset fit inside ~$400-500K cash down (e.g., Houston Super-Sized laundromat, Cedar Rapids car wash+RE, Tampa vending route). (3) CANADIAN financing (BDC / Canadian banks) really only helps if he buys a CANADIAN laundromat/storage/car wash — BDC and Canadian banks do not conveniently mortgage a US hard asset for him. (4) Conventional US commercial bank / credit union is possible but wants a US entity, US credit history, 25-40% down, and often a US guarantor — a fallback, not a base case. FLAG: any deal that 'only pencils with SBA-style leverage' should be treated as out of reach; prefer deals that work all-cash or with a seller note secured by the equipment/real estate.",
      "fit": "Strong fit for the diligence and optimization side; neutral on the physical ops. Hooman's biggest edge in this category is DILIGENCE ALPHA: the #1 way to avoid overpaying (or buying a lemon) is verifying true cash volume, and for laundromats/car washes that is a data task — regressing water/sewer/electric utility bills against reported revenue to detect inflated SDE, which he can do far better than 99% of buyers. For vending it's per-machine sell-through and route-optimization analytics (dynamic restocking, location scoring) — directly in his wheelhouse. His EE background + mech-eng friends help with equipment assessment (laundry machine age, car-wash pumps/reclaim, gate/keypad systems). Where his AI/data edge is largely IRRELEVANT: the day-to-day is collections, maintenance calls, attendant/driver management, and lease/landlord relations — these are people/ops skills, not technical. Value-creation upside he could actually build: card/app payment + remote monitoring retrofit on an older cash laundromat (raises price, adds data, reduces skim), dynamic pricing on storage/wash, and analytics-driven vending route optimization. Net: he can absolutely run and improve these (especially if he goes full-time), and his analytical edge is a real acquisition advantage, but the moat/return comes from the asset + a good buy price, not from software he writes.",
      "verdict": "Yes for LAUNDROMATS specifically; mixed-to-weak for the rest. Laundromats are the strongest ~$500K vein: uniquely they are simultaneously cash-fit for a non-SBA Canadian buyer, high-yield (real ~3x SDE deals throw off 15-25%), semi-absentee, AI-/recession-safe, and directly diligenceable with Hooman's data skills (regress water/sewer/electric utility bills against reported revenue to catch inflated 'cash flow'). Best sub-play = a laundromat bought all-cash or with a seller note, chosen on VERIFIED utility data + a 10+ year secure lease + recent equipment. Self-storage is the better long-term asset (appreciating, most passive, pricing power) but the worst fit at $500K without SBA leverage — quality facilities are real-estate-priced at 5-7% caps and $1M+, so all-cash yield is only ~6%; it would only work as a small Canadian facility with BDC/bank debt. Car washes (self-serve) are cash-fit and high-yield but the most operationally fragile (maintenance, weather, a new tunnel next door). Vending/ATM is cheapest and easiest to enter but the weakest moat/durability. Net: pursue laundromats hard, cherry-pick one self-serve car wash with real estate, treat storage as a Canadian-only or note-only play, and use vending only as a low-stakes 'learn ops' entry.",

      "economics": "Typical multiples: 2.0-3.0x SDE for owner-operated niche manufacturers, sign/print shops, and small distributors; commodity distributors and delivery routes ask a richer 4-5x but are usually overpriced. Cash yield: a fair ~$370-550K all-cash buy at 2.4-2.75x SDE produces $155K-$200K SDE/yr (~$13K-$17K/mo) pre-tax = roughly 31-40% cash-on-cash on $500K — BUT SDE bundles the full-time owner's wage, so treat only about half as true return on capital and half as pay for your labor.     {
      "category": "Franchises / multi-unit / semi-absentee ownership",
      "economics": "Small franchise resales trade ~2.0-3.0x SDE (Duck Donuts ~2.7x on $187K SDE; Koala ~1.9x; Budget Blinds ~2.7x).       "financing": "SBA 7(a)/504 is OFF the table for Hooman (requires US citizen or lawful permanent resident). (b) SELLER NOTE / vendor take-back — common on franchise resales (10-30%, 3-5yr), realistic way to stretch to $600-700K or preserve cash; franchisor still must approve the buyer. FLAG: operating a US franchise hands-on as a Canadian likely needs an E-2 treaty-investor visa; passive/remote ownership needs a genuine US manager. Cleanest fit = a CANADIAN franchise resale (BDC + seller VTB, no visa/tax friction) — but the deals captured here are US listings, so a dedicated Canadian scan (Sunbelt Canada, businessesforsale.com/canada, CFA member resales) is warranted before committing.",
      "fit": "Edge helps most in home services with route density, scheduling, and CRM (Pool Maintenance, Budget Blinds, Koala, mobile floor covering) — his analytics + marketing-automation can lift a sleepy unit's lead-gen and utilization, and physical presence is optional. His diligence alpha (reading an FDD, cohort-analyzing recurring revenue, correctly pricing royalty drag) is a real advantage in buying well. Time: to keep the Adobe job he needs a genuinely manager-run multi-unit (rare and pricier at this budget); otherwise these are hands-on, full-time owner-operator businesses.",
      "verdict": "MEDIUM vein — real cash flow exists but structurally poor fit for THIS buyer. Three stacked headwinds: (1) No SBA means he pays full ~$500K ALL-CASH while the market is priced for leveraged US buyers putting 10% down — franchise units are the canonical SBA-financed asset class, so this is the category most penalized by his citizenship. technical edge is a genuine *value-creation* lever, not decoration. Best target: **EH&S / SDS
compliance SaaS, $325K / $110K SDE / ~3x** — mandate-driven sticky demand, ~$175K cash left for a

/ cut infra cost to re-accelerate. Runs ~part-time, leaving room to build.

**#3 — A recurring-ROUTE local service business (pest control / pool route).** Cheap 2.0–2.8x SDE,
30–45% yields, AI-safe, delegable to techs. Best all-cash target: **Camden NJ pest control, $500K /
$180K SDE, 1000+ residual contracts, 40-yr track record** (the contract book is the moat). No trade
license (applicator exam only). Full-time-ish, but real recurring cash flow.

**#4 — Signage/CNC/plastics fabrication + supplies, $370K / $155K SDE / 2.39x (Buncombe NC).**
Cheapest fair-value operating business in the scan, three diversified revenue streams, and it
overlaps his CutLog/laser domain — genuine familiarity + quoting/inventory-automation upside. But
it is a hands-on full-time operator job, not a software company.

**#5 (highest raw yield, highest risk) — Signage-materials-tier physical asset arbitrage:**
the Houston "super-sized" laundromat ($650K/$230K SDE, ~2.8x) or 2 self-serve car washes ($450K/
$166K SDE, ~37% yield). Higher cash, but unverified SDE and lease/equipment fragility — only after
brutal utility-data diligence and a seller note to offload risk.

- **SBA 7(a)/504 is OFF the table.** SBA SOP 50 10 (reinforced by the March 2025 EO 14159 change)

  Canadian citizen with no US green card cannot use it. **VERIFY his exact residency first** — but
  base case = no SBA.
- **What that costs him:** the entire US small-biz market is priced for leveraged buyers putting
  ~10% down. With the SAME $500K cash, a US buyer reaches a **$1–2M** business (10% down + SBA 90%).
  Hooman reaches only a **~$500K all-cash** business — roughly **3–4x smaller SDE** for the same cash
  out of pocket. Franchises, storage, car-wash-with-RE, and higher-ticket HVAC/pest are the deals
  most distorted by this (their asking prices assume leverage he can't get).
- **His only real leverage = a SELLER NOTE / vendor take-back** (10–50%, paid from the business's

  diligence item for any US operator business, and a reason SaaS/remote/semi-absentee assets are

blocker); no cash buffer at $500K all-cash. The 1000-contract book is the durable moat.

hr/wk. *Edge REAL:* direct CutLog/CNC domain overlap; quoting automation, inventory/demand

managing 6 staff. *What goes wrong:* full-time operator job (not a software company), leased space,
